```{r}
#| label: packages

# check packages
packages <- c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "modelsummary",
              "quarto", "usethis", "gitcreds")
missing <- packages[!sapply(packages, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  stop("Please install the following package(s): ",
       paste(missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: versions

# quarto
quarto_version <- readLines(file.path(Sys.getenv("QUARTO_SHARE_PATH"), "version"))[1]
quarto_ok <- package_version(quarto_version) >= "1.7"

# git
git <- suppressWarnings(tryCatch(
  system2("git", "--version", stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE),
  error = function(e) ""))
git_ok <- length(git) > 0 && grepl("^git version", git[1])

# packages
package_versions <- paste0("`", packages, "` ",
                           sapply(packages, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p))),
                           collapse = ", ")
```

# Congratulations!

If you are reading this in a PDF document, your computer is ready to turn Quarto documents into PDF, with R, Quarto, and LaTeX working together.

# Your setup

```{r}
#| label: setup-report
#| output: asis

cat("-   R: ", R.version.string, "\n", sep = "")
cat("-   Quarto: version ", quarto_version,
    if (quarto_ok) " --- up to date" else
      " --- **please update RStudio, or install the latest version of Quarto**",
    "\n", sep = "")
cat("-   Git: ", if (git_ok) git[1] else "**not found --- please install Git**",
    "\n", sep = "")
cat("-   Packages: ", package_versions, "\n\n", sep = "")

cat(if (quarto_ok && git_ok)
      "Everything is ready. There is nothing else to do --- see you at the workshop!"
    else
      "Almost there: please see the item(s) in bold above, and the preparation guide.")
```
